skill.name: gh-cli
skill.description: A comprehensive GitHub CLI reference that helps agents use gh for repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, releases, projects, gists, codespaces, and account operations.
skill.summary: Use GitHub CLI commands safely and accurately across common GitHub workflows.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: The skill is a large Markdown reference for GitHub CLI usage, so many static command findings are documentation examples rather than hidden executable code. Real risks remain where examples use sudo, write shell completion files, export GitHub tokens, or perform bulk mutating GitHub operations; these require user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Privileged installation commands are presented as runnable examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings that sudo installation steps require user approval and should not be run automatically by an agent.

remediation.issue: Token examples show GH_TOKEN assignment and token export commands.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token-looking placeholders with clearly non-secret placeholders and warn users not to paste real tokens into shared prompts or logs.

remediation.issue: Bulk mutation examples can change many issues, pull requests, or project records.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend dry-run review steps and require explicit repository and item confirmation before executing bulk gh commands.

remediation.issue: Shell completion examples write files in the user home directory or evaluate generated shell output.
remediation.suggestion: Document that shell configuration changes should be reviewed by the user before being applied.

content.value_statement: GitHub CLI has many commands, flags, and workflows that are hard to remember. This skill gives Claude and other coding agents a structured gh reference for common GitHub operations.
actual_capabilities: Provides gh command examples for authentication, repositories, issues, pull requests, and releases.
Covers GitHub Actions workflows, runs, artifacts, secrets, variables, and caches.
Explains GitHub Projects, gists, codespaces, organizations, and extensions through CLI examples.
Shows formatting options such as JSON output, jq filters, templates, and pagination.
Includes troubleshooting guidance and links to official GitHub CLI documentation.
limitations: It is a reference document, not an executable wrapper around gh.
Commands that mutate GitHub state still require user review and permissions.
Some examples use placeholders that must be replaced with real repository or account values.
It does not verify current GitHub CLI version behavior at runtime.

use_cases.title: Prepare pull request work
use_cases.description: Find the right gh commands to inspect, create, edit, merge, or review pull requests.

use_cases.title: Operate repository workflows
use_cases.description: Use gh commands for Actions runs, releases, repository settings, secrets, and variables.

use_cases.title: Triage GitHub activity
use_cases.description: List, filter, label, assign, close, and search issues or discussions from the command line.

prompt_templates.title: Find a basic gh command
prompt_templates.prompt: Which gh command should I use to list open pull requests in this repository?

prompt_templates.title: Build a safe issue triage command
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a gh command to find open issues with the bug label, but do not close or edit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a failed workflow run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gh CLI reference to show how to inspect the latest failed GitHub Actions run and download its logs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a repository automation workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe sequence of gh commands to label stale pull requests after I review the candidates. Include confirmation steps before mutation.

output_examples.input: Show me how to inspect a pull request before merging.
output: Suggests commands to view the pull request, checks, files, reviews, and status.
Calls out which commands are read-only and which commands merge or modify state.

output_examples.input: I need to debug a failed GitHub Actions run.
output: Provides a sequence to list runs, view run details, inspect jobs, and download logs.
Mentions that rerun or cancel commands change workflow state.

output_examples.input: Help me create a release from the command line.
output_examples.output: Explains how to draft, upload assets, view, and publish a GitHub release with gh while checking tags and notes first.

best_practices: Run read-only gh commands first, then confirm before commands that edit or delete GitHub data.
Use explicit repository, owner, and branch arguments when operating outside the current directory.
Keep tokens out of prompts, terminal logs, and shared command history.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk edit or delete commands without reviewing the target list first.
Do not paste real access tokens into examples or issue comments.
Do not run sudo installation steps unless the user explicitly approves host changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run GitHub CLI commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance. Any command execution depends on the host agent and user approval settings.

faq.question: Can it help with pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands for listing, viewing, creating, editing, reviewing, checking, and merging pull requests.

faq.question: Can it manage GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers workflows, runs, jobs, logs, artifacts, secrets, variables, and caches.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: It can be used with private repositories, but users must protect tokens and review commands that expose or mutate private data.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub Enterprise?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference includes hostname options and examples for GitHub Enterprise environments.

faq.question: What should I review before using generated commands?
faq.answer: Check the repository, branch, IDs, labels, and whether the command changes GitHub state or local shell configuration.
